(p-٢٣٤) **Surah al-ʿAṣr**

The Imam al-Shafiʿi, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It is a surah which, if nothing had been sent down to mankind but it, would have sufficed them." This is the meaning of the words of another scholar: "It comprises all the sciences of the Qur'an. Its aim is to honour the human species, created from a clinging clot, and to explain its essence and quintessence, namely the saved party on the Day of questioning about the purity of deeds, after an indication to their opposites, and an informing about what saves from deeds and states, through abandoning the perishable and turning to the enduring, because it is the essence of existence and the kernel of being. Its name, al-ʿAṣr, is clear in this respect, for al-ʿAṣr (the pressing) extracts the essence of what is pressed and distinguishes its purity. For this reason the time of this final Prophet, who is the essence of creation, was the time of al-ʿAṣr, and the prayer of al-ʿAṣr was the most excellent of the prayers. The explanation of its inclusion of the sciences of the Qur'an is that its whole is an interpretation of [what -] al-Ghazali said: The Qur'an is like a sea in which there are islands (p-٢٣٥) with six kinds of mines, four of which are important. Two of the important ones are: a most excellent ruby, its red part for the knowledge of Allah, its green part for His attributes, and its blue part for His acts; and an emerald, green, which is knowledge of the Last Day and what is in it. Two others, the first of which is a radiant pearl, which is knowledge of the acts of worship that bring one near to Him, glorified and exalted be He; and the second of which is a fragrant musk, which is knowledge of the customs by which acts of worship are prepared. Two complete ones: a greatest antidote, which is knowledge of removing doubts, dubious claims and illusions, for these are poisons and destroyers of religion; and a white ambergris, which is taking lessons from those who perished, by avoiding what was the cause of their destruction, and following those who were saved by adhering to what was the cause of their salvation. The first category is for the ambergris, for in it is the smelling of the scents of the one who perished and of his opposite, the one who was saved. It was begun with because the repelling of harms takes precedence over the attainment of benefits. The second category is for the ruby with its three attributes and for the emerald. The third is for the pearl and the musk, which are intended acts of worship and customs that serve as extended means to them. The fourth is for the antidote, because doubts and suspicions only arise from vain illusions and false imaginings. The fifth is a means to them and a completion of them, because knowing that and avoiding it cannot be achieved except by exerting effort in patience." In the name of Allah, (p-٢٣٦) "Everything perishes except His Face" the Most Merciful, "by whose blessing the righteous and the wicked are alike covered, so nothing resembles Him," the Most Compassionate, "who specially granted the completion of blessing to His friends, so they became the brightness of the age and the forehead of its people."

* *

Since the enjoyment of this apparent worldly life lies in luxuriating in its goods, and since man is accountable for what he witnesses, the surah of al-Takathur concluded concerning that bliss, threatening with the vision of the Blazing Fire. So the dweller of this abode is in the utmost peril, and his bliss is in the utmost turbidity. He said, indicating by this that most people are lost, emphasizing with the oath and the particle what is due to the majority's denial of this, either by speech or by state: ﴿By time﴾, that is, the time in which its origin, Adam, peace be upon him, was created, and it was at the afternoon of Friday, as stated in the authentic hadith in Muslim; or the middle prayer, or its time, which is the time of the bearer of this Law, whose measure of the past time equals the measure of the time of al-ʿAṣr of the day or part of it; or the time of every person, which is the essence in relation to him, alerting him to its preciousness, pointing to the need to seize the opportunity to spend it in good, out of fear of the Gathering; or the time of the late afternoon, because it is the best of it, by what it contains of freedom from occupations, facing rest, and attaining the benefit of what one spent that day on; [and] by what it indicates of the length of the hour and the profit of one who had merchandise in it, by the conclusion of deeds and the ending of the day; and what indicates the Resurrection; or the whole of the age in which Allah, glorified and exalted be He, brought the creatures into existence and decreed the decreed matters, by the wonders that appeared in it indicating the might and greatness that Allah, exalted be He, possesses, which call one to direct the aspiration towards Him and confine it to Him (p-٢٣٧).

﴿Indeed, mankind﴾, that is, this species, which is the noblest of species because it was created in the best form, just as al-'Asr (time) is the essence of time, and al-'Asr is for extracting the essences of things. ﴿Is indeed in loss﴾, that is, in deficiency, according to their endeavours toward their desires and their spending of their lifetimes on their aims, because of their natural inclination toward the present, their turning away from the unseen, and their being deceived by the transient. The loss may be small or great, according to the varying of people into the intelligent and the vile. Whoever is a disbeliever is in ingratitude (kufran), and whoever is a believer but a disobedient sinner is in loss (khusran) if he goes to excess in disobedience; otherwise he is in loss in its absolute sense, which is the meaning of the bare verbal noun. In this there is an indication of knowledge of the need for the sending of Messengers to explain what pleases Allah of beliefs, acts of worship, and customs, in faith, Islam, and their continuance, so that its doer will be of the grip of the right hand and its abandoner of the companions of the left.

Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, the Ustadh (teacher), said: When the Exalted said ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has distracted you﴾ [al-Takathur: 1], this included an indication of the deficiency of human vision and the confinement of his perception to the immediate rather than the deferred, in which lies his success and salvation. That is because of his distance from knowledge of what the nature requires. ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72]. He, glory be to Him, informed that this is the condition of man by virtue of being man, so He said ﴿By time﴾ [al-'Asr: 1], ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾. So deficiency is his condition, wrongdoing is his nature, and ignorance is his disposition, so it is fitting that rivalry in increase should distract him, and Allah does not place in him the spirit of faith, ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-'Asr: 3] to the end of it. These are those whom ﴿neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Nur: 37]. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 103, verse 3:

When a judgment is passed on the species, it is a judgment on all of them, since they have nothing of their own essence except that. Among them, however, were those whom Allah, glorified and exalted, purified from what man was created with, by making him in the best of forms and preserving him from inclination despite the deficiencies within him. He, glorified and exalted, made an exception for them, because they are very few relative to the people of loss. So He said, indicating through the exception that souls are inclined to evil and given over to idleness and frivolity, and that the sincere one is one in a thousand as in the sound hadith: ﴿Except those who believe﴾. That is, they brought about faith (iman), which is affirmation of what is known by necessity to have been brought by the Prophet (ﷺ): the Oneness of Allah, glorified and exalted, and affirmation of His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day. Perhaps the wisdom in expressing it in the past tense is to urge entry into the religion even at its lowest degree, and to give good news to whoever does this, on its condition, of salvation from loss.

(p-239) Since man is a rational animal, and the perfection of his animality lies in the practical faculty (al-quwwah al-'amaliyyah) for movement by will rather than by the compelling dictates of brutish desire, Allah said: ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾. That is, as confirmation of what they professed of faith. ﴿The righteous deeds﴾, that is, this category, which is following the commands and avoiding the prohibitions, in acts of worship such as prayer and in customary matters such as trade. Thus by this they became Muslims (muslimin) after having been believers (mu'minin), and they preferred the Hereafter over this world, so that abundance did not distract them, and they succeeded in eternal life and everlasting happiness, and nothing of loss touched them.

[Since man, after his own perfection through deeds, is not wholly freed from loss] except by perfecting others, and then he becomes an heir, because the prophets, upon them be blessings and peace, were sent for the sake of perfecting others; religion does not stand, and when it stands it is not complete except through commanding right and forbidding wrong, which arises from the light of the heart; and this cannot be achieved except through collective effort. He said, specifying what is included among the righteous deeds in order to alert to its greatness: ﴿and enjoined one another﴾, that is, some of them urged others, by the tongue of state or of speech: ﴿to truth﴾, that is, the established matter, which is everything the Law has judged to be valid, so that nothing that negates it is sound, whether in speech, deed, belief, or other, whether action or abstention. Thus they were doers of good (muhsinin), and the perfection in the practical faculty is through bringing about what is good.

(p-240) Since man [tends] toward deficiency, the doer of that good is exposed to hatred from the people of enmity, who are the majority in every age, He said: ﴿and enjoined one another﴾, because man is roused by admonition, and the glance and the word benefit him, ﴿to patience﴾, that is, the patience arising from the purification of the soul in acting in obedience to Allah, including upholding the truth and nullifying falsehood and negating it and its people, and patience in what befalls one because of that by way of harm, by avoiding evils, until death, which is the means that conveys one to the Abode of Peace. Thus they were completing the practical faculty and preserving what preceded it of the cognitive faculty. This is the wisdom of acts of worship, for the wisdom of a thing is its purpose and the intended benefit from it. Here it is two things: one external to the doer, which is Paradise, and one internal and residing in him, which is the light brought near to the Truth, glorified and exalted. The expression "enjoining" (al-wasiyyah) was chosen to indicate gentleness in commanding right and forbidding wrong, and using softness to the utmost effort. Patience is the essence of man, his secret, his purity, his cream and his extract, which cannot be reached except by man compelling himself and forcing it to the acts of obedience and subduing it to adhere to the Sunnah and the community, until patience becomes for it a habit and a craft through training. Thus its last part embraces its first, and its joint connects with its conveyor, (p-241) and these are fourteen words, pointing to the fact that in the fourteenth year of prophethood there is permission for jihad, which is the head of enjoining right by action, to make the truth manifest. This is the year of the Hijrah in which its full moon appeared, its light and status spread, its might and victory multiplied. If you add to them four words, the Basmalah, they match in number the year five of the Hijrah, in which occurred the Battle of Badr al-Mawid and the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), and in both of them the Prophet (ﷺ) displayed the most complete patience, and then those of the Companions who agreed with him, may Allah be pleased with them, to make the truth and rightness manifest. At Badr they were let down by the caravan of 'Abd al-Qays, or by Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud, and by the agreement of the hypocrites, and they were frightened until terror and cowardice almost overwhelmed them all. So the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"By Allah, I will go out even if no one goes out with me." And Allah revealed concerning it: ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them," but it increased them in faith and they said﴾ [Al 'Imran: 173], and the verses that follow. At the Confederates, "the eyes turned aside and the hearts reached the throats," and the outcome of patience in it was made manifest in what the Prophet (ﷺ) said when they had departed: "Now we shall attack them, and they will not attack us." If you add to them the four pronouns, they point to the year nine, in which was the Expedition of Tabuk, which is the Expedition of Hardship (al-'Usrah), because of [what was] (p-242) in it of hardship, the outcome of patience in which was the arrival of delegations, with the magnificence of might and high lineage, and the continuous succession of good fortunes, by the gentle kindness of the Compassionate, the Loving, and by this came the light of existence, and the continuous succession of bounty and generosity from the God who is worshipped. And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, and his family and companions, the best of existence.
